skill.name: parallel-task-spark
skill.description: Coordinates parallel coding subagents from a markdown plan, using task dependencies to launch, validate, log, and commit work in waves.
skill.summary: Runs dependency-aware development plan tasks through parallel Sparky subagents.
skill.author: am-will

content.value_statement: Large implementation plans are slow when tasks are handled one by one. This skill launches dependency-ready tasks through Sparky subagents and records progress in the plan.
actual_capabilities: Parses markdown plan files for task IDs, names, dependencies, and acceptance criteria.
Filters execution to requested task subsets and their required dependencies.
Launches unblocked Sparky subagents in parallel waves.
Checks subagent results for completion, validation, and plan updates.
Requests retries or escalation when a task is not complete.
Produces an execution summary with completed tasks, issues, files, and next steps.
limitations: Requires recognizable markdown task headings and depends_on lists.
Requires Sparky subagent support in the host environment.
Does not define conflict handling for overlapping file edits.
Validation depends on tests and commands available in the project.

use_cases.title: Execute Implementation Plans
use_cases.description: Break a prepared engineering plan into dependency-safe waves and run ready tasks in parallel.

use_cases.title: Speed Up Independent Work
use_cases.description: Run selected independent tasks from a plan while preserving dependencies and completion logs.

use_cases.title: Track Multi-Agent Progress
use_cases.description: Review task outputs, validation status, modified files, and blockers after each execution wave.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Full Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for all eligible tasks in one plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use /parallel-task-spark with plans/implementation-plan.md. Run the full plan, follow task dependencies, and update the plan logs.

prompt_templates.title: Run Selected Tasks
prompt_templates.scenario: Limit execution to specific tasks and their required prerequisites.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use /parallel-task-spark with plans/auth-plan.md for tasks T1, T2, and T4. Include required dependencies and summarize validation.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a Risky Wave
prompt_templates.scenario: Ask for careful validation and escalation on a complex plan section.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use /parallel-task-spark with plans/migration-plan.md for the database tasks. Run dependency-ready work and escalate blockers before later waves.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Parallel Completion
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for execution plus strict review before continuing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use /parallel-task-spark with plans/release-plan.md. After each wave, inspect outputs, verify plan logs, confirm commits, and retry incomplete tasks.

output_examples.output: Execution summary with assigned tasks, completed work, issues, blocked items, files modified, validation status, and next steps.
A focused run report covering selected tasks, included dependencies, completion notes, and any deferred validation.

output_examples.input: Run the migration plan with parallel-task-spark and stop on blockers.
output_examples.output: Wave-by-wave status showing completed tasks, escalated blockers, retries requested, and plan log updates.

best_practices: Use clear task IDs, task names, dependencies, acceptance criteria, and validation steps in the plan.
Keep tasks independent when possible to reduce file conflicts between parallel subagents.
Review each wave summary before starting later tasks that depend on completed work.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill with vague plans that lack task boundaries or dependency data.
Do not assign overlapping file edits to parallel tasks without a conflict strategy.
Do not skip review of subagent outputs before launching dependent tasks.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It reads a markdown development plan, finds unblocked tasks, and coordinates Sparky subagents in dependency-safe waves.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it run every task at once?
faq.answer: No. It runs only tasks whose dependencies are complete, then repeats with the next unblocked wave.

faq.question: Can I run only part of a plan?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide task IDs, and the skill includes those tasks plus required dependencies.

faq.question: Does it validate the work?
faq.answer: It instructs subagents to run feasible validation and asks the orchestrator to inspect results before continuing.

faq.question: Does it push changes to a remote repository?
faq.answer: No. The skill explicitly tells subagents to commit only their own work and never push.
